ai.description: Amboli Day Gecko reaches 40 mm snout-vent length. It is brownish-grey with a distinct yellow-spotted vertebral stripe and a white-tipped tail. Key features include granular scales and webbed digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Amboli Day Gecko is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange vertebral stripe that runs along its back, contrasting with its dark body.
ai.habitat: The Amboli Day Gecko inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Northern Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations between 600 and 800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Amboli Day Gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small insects on tree trunks and rock surfaces within its restricted forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis amboliensis* is oviparous, laying a single hard-shelled egg per clutch. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Amboli Day Gecko is endemic to the northern Western Ghats, specifically inhabiting the Amboli region of Maharashtra at elevations between 600 and 800 meters.
